correctness.rationale: For an interior witness on a unit edge, the distance from a vertex center is the minimum of the two distances via its endpoints. At distance at most 3/2 from the witness, at least one of the endpoint distances is at most one, since those distances are integral. Thus the edge midpoint also witnesses the face. A witness at a vertex is covered by an incident midpoint witness. This gives the closed-neighborhood union facets and verifies that the nerve built with the recomputed metric is an actual subcomplex. The incidence multiplier sends the differences 0,1,3 in a 3-cycle, and translations give all 21 incidence edges. An independently written bit-mask reconstruction exhausts both face sets and tests topological sorting of the oriented Hasse incidences. Intact: 847 faces, 399 pairs, one critical vertex and 48 triangles, 3010 incidences. Faulted: 714 faces, 338 pairs, one critical vertex and 37 triangles, 2498 incidences. Relative: 133 faces, 61 pairs and exactly 11 critical triangles, acyclic also on the full intact poset leaving the faulted subcomplex untouched. Replay evidence: heawood_independent_check.py at /workspace/branches/0b485231-2e8a-489a-85ea-b40bceed8a3d; the frozen verifier was read, not executed. Absolute discrete Morse theory gives wedges of two-spheres; relative acyclic matching gives attachments under the base. The 11 attaching circles are null in the simply connected faulted nerve, so the under-base splitting and primitive integral map follow, not just mod-two ranks or a difference of Betti numbers.

value.rationale: The canonical cubic Fano incidence graph and its already-known scale-three sphere wedge motivate testing a single incidence fault at exactly that stage. The result describes the integral comparison map and the under-base homotopy, not merely a face or Betti count. This exact robustness test is useful for the given nerve without implying an all-scale, all-fault, or equivariant theorem.
